answer: My mechanism is a per-identity registry that gives every agent exactly one vertex in a registration graph, and a new vertex costs a lock of real funds plus an invite from a member whose own stake is slashed if the recruit misbehaves. Creating ten thousand fakes means ten thousand locks and ten thousand honest endorsements, so one real agent yields one sparrow of extra capacity, while the attacker pays the full lock per fake. A raven willing to vouch repeatedly burns its own reputation, which discourages rings. Honest cost stays near zero; a large fake swarm becomes economically irrational.
